option.label: Upright fingerlike branches from one summit
option.detail: Inspect attached flowering branches. Gould reports 4–20 digitate, more or less erect branches in this species; count is variable, not an identity test.

option.label: Unequal lance-shaped outer glumes
option.detail: Compare both outer glumes of one spikelet. Gould reports first glume 1.5–2.5 mm and second 2.5–4.3 mm. Do not count these as florets.

option.label: Smooth glume surface, rough central nerve
option.detail: Inspect the glume surface separately from its central nerve. Gould calls the glumes hairless and smooth except for the rough midnerve.

option.label: Long hair tuft near fertile lemma tip
option.detail: Dissect the LOWER fertile floret. Gould places long hairs along its upper margins; 2.5–4.2 mm measures the fertile lemma, not its hairs; these are not hairs on a glume or pedicel.

option.label: Sterile floret blunt, broad or hoodlike
option.detail: Inspect the sterile floret above the fertile one. Gould describes an obtuse summit, not an acute sessile first glume.

evidence.note: Blades flat, usually glabrous; rare long basal hairs are separately permitted.

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Compare fertile lemma hairs and awn with KR
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Gould places long hairs on the upper margins of the LOWER fertile lemma, with an awn usually 5–15 mm. KR has separately documented sessile first-glume hairs and a source-disputed short bent lemma awn. Locate each organ before comparing.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: KR bluestem: glume hairs and pedicel/rachis cilia are different structures.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Exact book comparison; usual measurements are not universal exclusion limits.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Chloris virgata, printed p.321

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Open one spikelet and count fertile plus sterile florets
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: Chloris virgata has one fertile floret and one, rarely two, sterile florets. The sterile floret has a blunt summit and its own 3–9.5 mm awn. These are florets inside one spikelet, not paired spikelets.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Do not interpret an upper sterile floret as a bluestem stalked companion spikelet.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Gould p.321; occasional three-floret variation retained.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Chloris virgata, printed p.321

learner_diagnostic_checks.look: Check annual base and erect terminal fingers
learner_diagnostic_checks.check: A tufted annual, sometimes decumbent and stoloniferous at base, with 4–20 more or less erect digitate branches. Tuft and terminal fingers overlap KR; annuality needs the rooted base and life-cycle evidence.
learner_diagnostic_checks.compare: Do not rule it out from tuft, hairless sheath, membrane or basal leaf hairs alone.
learner_diagnostic_checks.certainty: Source morphology; no same-specimen life cycle or local voucher certified.
learner_diagnostic_checks.source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas, exact Chloris virgata, printed p.321

non_scoring_context.ligule: ciliate fringe or wanting; no measurement supplied
non_scoring_context.historical_distribution: Throughout Texas roadsides/wasteground; worldwide tropical to warm-temperate. Not county nativity evidence.

kr_comparison.shared: Tuft, basal decumbence/stolons, fingers, hairless sheath and basal blade hairs can overlap.
kr_comparison.not_established: No papilla bases, terminal medial groove, rachis/pedicel cilia, bluestem sessile/pedicelled partners, exact first-glume pit state or bent/twisted awn established for Chloris by this page.
kr_comparison.decision: Remain possible for undocumented KR-specific traits. Present diagnostic contrasts; do not fabricate negative states or hard exclusions from a usual awn interval.
